concept: Higher-order product formulas trade depth for accuracy
summary: First-order Trotterization is shallow and simple but converges slowly; second-order symmetric formulas reduce leading error terms while increasing per-step circuit cost.
applies_to: accuracy-sensitive simulations with moderate backend depth
limitations: Second-order formulas can still be too deep for noisy hardware at high precision.
Higher order does not remove the need to reason about Hamiltonian decomposition.
implications: Prefer first-order formulas for baseline or shallow-depth checks.
Prefer second-order formulas when first-order error is unacceptable and depth budget allows.
Escalate to more advanced algorithms when required precision makes Trotter depth impractical.

evidence.note: Foundational source for systematic product-formula approximants.
Studies symmetry-based decompositions that reduce error and improve robustness under noise.
